best_for: Parents and teachers of children aged 2 to 10 who want a free, ad-free set of learning games on a family or classroom PC.
description:
GCompris is a set of learning games for young children, hosted and developed by the KDE community. It is also an official GNU package, and its copyright notice, shared by Timothée Giet and others, goes back to 2000.

Your child can start with the basics of the computer itself, learning to use the keyboard, mouse and touchscreen. Then come letters, words and typing practice, numbers, sums and times tables, and science topics such as the water cycle, a canal lock and renewable energy. Geography activities cover countries and regions. For a break there are chess, memory, hangman, tic-tac-toe and align four, plus activities on colors, shapes, Braille and telling time on a clock.

points.title: More than 100 activities
points.text: GCompris covers ages 2 to 10 with over 100 activities, and the site offers it in dozens of languages.

points.title: Free software from KDE
points.text: It is AGPL open source and part of KDE. The project takes donations, and the desktop builds here need no account.

points.title: No current Mac version
points.text: The latest release is not built for macOS because the team lacks the setup to build and test it. Version 4.3 is the last Mac release, so Mac families need to stay on it.

points.title: 64-bit Windows 10 or 11
points.text: Version 26.2 is 64-bit only and needs Windows 10 or 11. Older PCs can use 4.3.1 in 32-bit, or 15.10 for Windows XP, from the GCompris site.

points.title: Linux and other devices
points.text: The Flatpak is verified on Flathub and published by KDE, for x64 and Arm64. The standalone Linux build needs kernel 5.15 and glibc 2.35. Android and Raspberry Pi builds are offered too.

points.title: Easy to roll out to a classroom
points.text: Both Windows installers, the .exe and the .msi, install for all users, which suits shared PCs. The Windows listing keeps 4 versions; Linux lists only the current release.
